(a) Selected chronic conditions consists of arthritis, asthma, back problems (dorsopathies), cancer (malignant neoplasms), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), diabetes mellitus, heart, stroke and vascular disease, kidney disease, mental and behavioural conditions and osteoporosis. Includes persons who have a current health condition which has lasted, or is expected to last, for 6 months or more; except for persons reporting diabetes mellitus and/or heart, stroke and vascular disease which are included irrespective of whether the condition is current and/or long-term. Multiple conditions belonging to the same condition type (e.g. mental and behavioural conditions) are treated as the one condition. For example, a person with anxiety and depression (and no other chronic condition) is treated as having one selected chronic condition. For more information see Methodology.
(b) Persons who have a current medical condition which has lasted, or is expected to last, for 6 months or more, unless otherwise stated.
(c) Includes rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, other and type unknown.
(d) Includes sciatica, disc disorders, back pain/problems not elsewhere classified and curvature of the spine.
(e) Includes chronic bronchitis, emphysema and chronic airflow limitation. Asthma is reported separately.
(f) Includes Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes mellitus, and type unknown. These estimates include persons who reported they had diabetes mellitus but that it was not current at the time of interview.

(g) Includes angina, heart attack, other ischaemic heart diseases, stroke and other cerebrovascular diseases, oedema or heart failure, and diseases of the arteries, arterioles and capillaries. Estimates include persons who reported they had angina, heart attack, other ischaemic heart diseases, stroke and other cerebrovascular diseases or heart failure but that these conditions were not current at the time of interview.
(h) Self-reported hypertension only, excludes measured high blood pressure.

(i) Includes harmful use or dependence on alcohol and/or drugs, mood (affective) disorders, anxiety related disorders, problems of psychological development, organic mental disorders and other mental and behavioural conditions.
(j) Includes self-reported mental and behavioural conditions only and is not based on any diagnostic screening tool. For more information, see Comparing ABS long-term health conditions data sources.
(l) National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) 2009 guideline 1 for the consumption of alcohol which recommends no more than 2 standard drinks per day. For more information see Methodology.
(m) NHMRC 2009 guideline 2 for the consumption of alcohol which recommends no more than 4 standard drinks on a single occasion. For more information see Methodology.
(n) Total includes persons who did not remember when they last consumed alcohol

(o) The Australian Adult Alcohol Guideline recommends persons aged 18 years and over, either drink no more than 10 standard drinks per week or no more than 4 standard drinks on a single day once a month or more often. For more information see Methodology.

(p) Body Mass Index is derived from measured height and weight. In 2022, 40.8% of respondents aged 18 years and over did not have their height, weight or both measured. For these respondents, imputation was used to obtain height, weight and BMI scores. For more information see Methodology.
(r) Total excludes persons who self-reported being pregnant at the time of interview.

(s) In 2022, 39.4% of respondents aged 18 years and over did not have their waist measured. For these respondents, imputation was used to obtain waist circumference. For more information see Methodology.
(t) A waist circumference of between 94cm and 101cm for males or between 80cm and 87cm for females.
(u) A waist circumference of 102 cm or more for males or 88 cm or more for females.

(v) National Health and Medical Research Council's (NHMRC) 2013 Australian Dietary Guidelines recommend a minimum number of serves of fruit and vegetables each day, depending on a person's age and sex, to ensure good nutrition and health. For more information see Methodology.

(w) Measured high blood pressure excludes self-reported hypertension prevalence rates. In 2022, 39.0% of respondents aged 18 years and over did not have their blood pressure measured. For these respondents, imputation was used to obtain blood pressure. For more information see Methodology.
(x) A score of 22 or more on the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K10). For more information see Methodology.
(y) Total excludes persons not present for interview.

(z) 2014 Physical activity guidelines are based on Australia’s Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour Guidelines and assessed against the respective age group. For more information see Methodology.

(aa) Physical activity excluding workplace activity refers to exercise which includes walking for transport, walking for fitness, sport or recreation, moderate exercise and/or vigorous exercise undertaken in the last week.
(ab) These estimates include persons who reported no walking for transport, walking for fitness, sport or recreation, moderate exercise and/or vigorous exercise.
